title: The htsglang development rig, as measured on it
caveat: Every number in this file was measured on ONE machine (5090 + 2x 3080, DDR4 host, ZFS on NVMe, 40G RoCE to rig-2). It is a rig profile, not a hardware truth: ANALYSE_389's own words about the 1.8 GB/s NVMe figure -- 'this verdict must not be recorded as a verdict on the approach' -- apply to every row here. A different rig loads a different profile; nothing in the registry hardcodes these values.
sources: DESIGN_407_memory_tier_registry.md section 1.1, which cites each figure to the runbook / EVAL / ANALYSE line it came from.

hardware.label: 1x RTX 5090:32GiB + 2x RTX 3080:20GiB
hardware.cards_note: EMPTY DELIBERATELY, and it is a functional statement rather than a TODO. With no card rows this profile has no exact hardware key, so it can only ever match at MODEL scope -- which licenses the device_models templates below and NOTHING else. Its host, filesystem and rig-2 tiers are therefore not applied on any machine, including the one they were measured on, until a session with cards writes the UUID rows here (memtier.fingerprint.hardware_block produces them). That is the correct default for a file that ships in the repository: a profile checked into a public tree must not be able to assert facts about a reader's host RAM or disks, and the two card MODEL templates are the only rows in it that generalise beyond one box.

total.source: NVML total 32607 MiB; rig-runbook.md:2977, DESIGN_407 section 1.1 T0. Live NVML overrides this at enumeration.

floor.source: the #330 pinned floor (weights, graphs, GDN pool, activation workspaces, allocator metadata) is measured once per boot as nvml_process_used_bytes - vmm_backed_bytes; it does not exist before a boot

latency_us.source: no device-memory point-latency probe exists in this tree; card_probe measures bandwidth only (DESIGN_407 section 4, M1)

aperture_bytes.source: the EFFECTIVE per-directed-pair BAR1 aperture is what #286's window policy needs; scripts/p2p_readiness/capability_matrix.py has never been run and no results/ directory exists (DESIGN_407 section 4, M2). The nominal ReBAR window is in properties and is NOT this number.

properties.peer_path_evidence: barlink vs NCCL, interleaved, bf16, three cards: 1.13 / 1.34 / 1.15 / 1.04 / 1.30x at 20 KiB / 80 KiB / 1 MiB / 4 MiB / 16 MiB (measured, commit 137e3a6c25). The smallest datapoint is a 20 KiB three-rank all_reduce at 45.59 us -- a COLLECTIVE, not a point latency.
properties.peer_latency_claim: the '1-3 us posted write' class quoted for peer VRAM is an ASSUMPTION (EVAL_p2p_prefill_decode_split.md:140, under 'Tragende Annahmen'), which is why caps.latency_us is absent rather than estimated

total.source: NVML total 20480 MiB; rig-runbook.md:2977, DESIGN_407 section 1.1 T0. Live NVML overrides this at enumeration.

floor.source: the #330 pinned floor is measured once per boot as nvml_process_used_bytes - vmm_backed_bytes; it does not exist before a boot

latency_us.source: no device-memory point-latency probe exists in this tree; card_probe measures bandwidth only (DESIGN_407 section 4, M1)

aperture_bytes.source: the EFFECTIVE per-directed-pair BAR1 aperture is unmeasured (DESIGN_407 section 4, M2); the nominal 256 MiB window and the 96 MiB that maps contiguously are in properties and must not be read as the effective aperture

properties.bar_size_irrelevant: #278 W1: BAR size moved nothing at any measured step, and the direct-vs-staged story is a BAND at 64-80 KiB rather than a crossover point

total.source: cgroup memory limit 98.5 GiB (MemTotal 103.3 GB, no swap); DESIGN_407 section 1.1 T2. Live /proc/meminfo + cgroup override this at enumeration.

floor.source: the non-ledger resident set at this tier (page cache, ARC, the TokenizerManager frontend process) is accounted nowhere -- #400's known blind spot, inherited unchanged. apply_local_facts() fills it from a live MemAvailable reading.

latency_us.source: no host-DRAM access-latency probe exists in this tree

bandwidth_gbs.source: central value of the measured 32-45 GB/s sustained band, ANALYSE_393_ik_llama.md:299-300. ESTIMATE and not MEASURED because the 51.2 GB/s peak it is read against is ASSUMED from dual-channel DDR4-3200 -- dmidecode -t 17 is empty under this VM. ANALYSE_393:554 names the measured read bandwidth as an open item (DESIGN_407 section 4, M4).

aperture_bytes.source: host RAM is not an aperture-gated tier

transport.name: pcie
transport.handle: torch pinned H2D/D2H; probe at rigmon/card_probe.py:561-586

properties.h2d_pinned_gbs: 6.4 / 13 / 13 per card (gen4 x4 / x8 / x8), aggregate 32.4 (measured, ANALYSE_393_ik_llama.md:301-304); barlink host-staged retake 14.3 / 6.5 / 13.2
properties.swap: none -- a swapless box, so an over-reservation here is an OOM kill and not a slowdown
properties.contention: all three rank processes contend for one memory controller; the per-card H2D figures were taken one direction at a time, alone
properties.rig_is_lower_bound: measured on this rig only; a machine with more channels moves this number and nothing in the registry assumes otherwise

total.source: free space at the time of the #389 measurement, ANALYSE_389_nvme_expert_tier.md:99. Live statvfs overrides this at enumeration.

floor.source: a filesystem tier holds no per-boot pinned floor; what is on it is on it

latency_us.source: no fio, no iodepth, no per-read microsecond figure exists anywhere in this tree; all of #389's arithmetic is bandwidth-only (DESIGN_407 section 4, M5)

bandwidth_gbs.source: cold read, iflag=direct, reproduced three times; ANALYSE_389_nvme_expert_tier.md:77-89, commit 71fc6356be

aperture_bytes.source: a filesystem is not an aperture-gated tier

properties.rewritable: yes -- #306 may rewrite a blob here in place, in a transformed representation, without the producer hearing about it
properties.arc_warm_excluded: the warm 3.8 / 9.5 GB/s readings are ARC hits and are deliberately NOT credited to this tier
properties.writeback_durability: unmeasured (DESIGN_407 section 4, M6): whether a write is durable when the call returns, and whether the page cache it leaves is reclaimable IN TIME, are open. Boot 8 died with memory.current at 98.3/98.5 GiB for seven minutes -- reclaimable is not reclaimable in time.
properties.page_cache_reclaim: posix_fadvise(DONTNEED) is a no-op for mapped pages and on this pool even post-unmap (16384/16384 pages resident by mincore, commit a8a2f7bc22); madvise(MADV_PAGEOUT) reclaims to 0
properties.hosts_hibernate_images: yes (#89). Hibernate images have no OFFLOAD_CLASSES member, so it is the persistent volatility class -- not the admits set -- that lets them rest here.
properties.rig_is_lower_bound: 1.8 GB/s is THIS box's ZFS-on-NVMe cold read; ANALYSE_389 is explicit that its K3 verdict must not be recorded as a verdict on the approach

total.source: a tmpfs has no measured constant size; it is a live statvfs fact, filled by apply_local_facts()

floor.source: a filesystem tier holds no per-boot pinned floor

bandwidth_gbs.source: no tmpfs bandwidth probe exists. This tier IS host RAM behind a filesystem API, but the host tier's DRAM figure is deliberately not copied here: a number measured on one path must not be reprinted under another path's name.

aperture_bytes.source: a filesystem is not an aperture-gated tier

properties.persistent_across_reboot: no -- this tier is the reason persistence is a DECLARED class and not an assumed property of a path. A --hibernate-dir pointed here yields a hibernate that does not survive a reboot, and nothing in the tree would notice (DESIGN_407 section 2.4b).
properties.backed_by: host:rig-1 -- bytes written here are charged to the host RAM budget, on a swapless box

total.source: rig-2's RAM has never been enumerated from this host; the registry does not guess a remote machine's size

floor.source: unknown for the same reason as total

latency_us.source: 8 B message on the 40G line; rig-runbook.md:1264. The 100G line measures 1.58 us and is slot-limited to 3.43 GB/s (PCIe-3.0-x4-bound).

bandwidth_gbs.source: staged RDMA at 1 MiB, EVAL_gdr_uebernahme.md:125. Same line: NCCL-over-sockets 2.07 GB/s, iperf3 single stream 1.93 GB/s.

health.reason: reachability is not probed at enumeration time in cut 1 -- the registry opens no socket to build a record. The last measured contact is the #266 cross-rig run; treat the tier as unreachable until a probe says otherwise.

properties.nic_relay_serialises: three pairs in parallel cost 2.34x latency for only 1.28x aggregate -- the single Gen3-x4 NIC is the wall (#278 V5). A remote tier is not width-scalable on this rig.
properties.collective_cost: at serving level, decode all_reduce ~89 us and verify all_reduce ~202 us, of which host staging carries ~86% (#266)
properties.ucx_barrier_us: 8.30 (world 2); all_reduce 8 KiB 44.92 us, 64 KiB 55.79 us, 512 KiB 237.70 us
properties.producer_fingerprint: a remote entry is a hit only if producer == consumer on model, quantization, KV dtype, TP size / rank-tp-ratio, DCP geometry, head geometry and layer count (#224). A mismatch is a hard request error, never silent corruption.
properties.line_pairing_warning: the 3.43 GB/s and 1.47 us figures quoted together in kv_session_spill_destination.destinations_error come from DIFFERENT lines (100G and 40G). DESIGN_407 open item 4: fix the string when cut 3 touches the function.
properties.rig_is_lower_bound: one 40G RoCE line through a Gen3-x4 slot; this is the wire this rig has, not the wire the approach needs

total.source: rig-2's cards have never been enumerated from this host

floor.source: rig-2's cards have never been enumerated from this host

latency_us.source: 8 B GDR direct into a 3080 BAR (staged: 3.77 us); EVAL_gdr_uebernahme.md:124. This is the INBOUND direction from rig-2's NIC, not a GPU-to-GPU path.

bandwidth_gbs.source: direct GDR into a 3080 BAR at 1 MiB vs 2.83 GB/s staged; #278's retake found no crossover point but a BAND at 64-80 KiB where direct loses, and direct winning outside it (20 KiB 1.26x, 1 MiB 1.19x, 4 MiB 1.24x)

aperture_bytes.source: unmeasured; #278 W1 also showed BAR size irrelevant at every measured step

health.reason: GPU-to-GPU across the rig boundary was never demonstrated on this hardware, and #280's userspace workaround is closed as impossible (cudaHostRegisterIoMemory -> CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE, driver guard osCheckGpuBarsOverlapAddrRange). Declared with a blocking verdict rather than omitted, so a rig where it works needs a data change and not a code change (DESIGN_407 X3).

properties.nordstern: this is the NORDSTERN shape (TP=5 across two rigs). Enumerating it with a blocking verdict makes the gap a dashboard row instead of an invisible absence.
properties.mr_registration_cost: untimed (DESIGN_407 section 4, M8): amortised to zero for a static pool, the whole design for anything dynamic

health.reason: never probed, in any unit. Reachable only through the rig-2 wire (DESIGN_407 section 4, M7), and declared here so the gap is visible rather than absent.

properties.flock: no -- flock does not cross the wire, which is why #89 needs a capability filter and not a filesystem-kind check
